overlap_rationale: Study A (Muchadenyika & Williams, 2018) and Study B (Marumahoko et al., 2020) are unrelated, empirically distinct studies conducted by completely separate research teams at different institutions, in different time periods, and using different designs and samples. Study A is a qualitative and institutional analysis based on 30 key-informant interviews conducted by Davison Muchadenyika in June–July 2013 ( primarily in Harare, Bulawayo, Masvingo, Mutare and Marondera) supplemented by secondary fiscal and Auditor-General records up to 2016, focusing on the centralisation of water/sanitation (ZINWA) and vehicle licensing (ZINARA). Study B is a post-Mugabe ('Second Republic', circa 2019) mixed-methods survey and fieldwork study across four purposively sampled urban local authorities (Bulawayo City Council, Chitungwiza Municipality, Zvishavane Town Council and Epworth Local Board), analyzing 100 usable closed-ended questionnaires (from 120 distributed), open-ended questionnaires, focus group discussions and in-depth interviews with municipal employees, officials and service consumers. Although both examine urban local governance and service delivery in Zimbabwe, they share no underlying primary empirical dataset or fieldwork sample.
study_a_sample_and_data: Qualitative key-informant interview study (N = 30 interviews conducted by Davison Muchadenyika in June–July 2013 across Harare, Bulawayo, Masvingo, Mutare and Marondera: 5 central government ministry officials, 6 local authority officials, 5 urban social movement actors, 3 political party representatives, 6 NGO/international agency staff and 5 planners/consultants/researchers), combined with secondary analysis of legislation, parliamentary reports and Auditor-General/fiscal data (2005–2016) on ZINWA water/sanitation centralisation and ZINARA vehicle licensing centralisation in urban Zimbabwe.
study_b_sample_and_data: Post-2017 ('Second Republic', circa 2019) mixed-methods primary survey and qualitative study across four purposively selected urban local authorities representing all four tiers of Zimbabwean urban councils (Bulawayo City Council, Chitungwiza Municipality, Zvishavane Town Council and Epworth Local Board). Primary data comprise N = 100 usable closed-ended questionnaires (out of 120 distributed to Ministry of Local Government officials, municipal employees and randomly selected service consumers), open-ended questionnaires, focus group discussions (5–10 participants per group, including UCAZ and Residents' Associations) and in-depth interviews with senior council managers.
